title: Add IngredientsView with scaling and checkbox state
description: Create IngredientsView.swift. Displays a list of Recipe.ingredients. A section header row shows 'Ingredients' on the leading edge and a Picker (bound to the external Scale binding) on the trailing edge. Each ingredient row has: a tappable circular checkbox (circle / checkmark.circle.fill) toggling local non-persistent 'gathered' state; the ingredient name (strikethrough + .secondary foreground when gathered); and the scaled quantity trailing, computed via RecipeScale.apply(to:). Empty state shows 'No ingredients listed' centered in .secondary foreground.
acceptance_criteria: Section header shows 'Ingredients' leading and scale Picker trailing bound to external binding.
Each row shows checkbox, name, and scaled quantity.
Tapping the checkbox toggles gathered state without persistence.
Gathered rows render name with .strikethrough() and .secondary foreground.
Quantities: .number scaled per RecipeScale rules, .text unchanged, nil hidden.
Empty state 'No ingredients listed' shown when Recipe.ingredients is empty.
Gathered state is non-persistent and resets when the view is re-initialised.

handoff_summary.completed: Implemented IngredientsView.swift at CookbookApp/Recipes/IngredientsView.swift. The view accepts `ingredients: [Ingredient]` and `@Binding var scale: RecipeScale`. Section header shows "Ingredients" leading and a `.menu`-style Picker trailing bound to the scale binding. Each row (private IngredientRow struct) has a checkbox Button (circle / checkmark.circle.fill SF symbols), ingredient name with conditional `.strikethrough()` and `.secondary` foreground, and scaled quantity trailing computed via `RecipeScale.apply(to:)` — nil quantities are hidden. Gathered state is `@State private var gathered: Set<Int>` keyed by ingredient index, so it resets on re-initialisation. Empty state renders "No ingredients listed" centered in `.secondary` foreground. Build verified: xcodebuild BUILD SUCCEEDED.
handoff_summary.remaining: None — all acceptance criteria are addressed.
handoff_summary.risks: Interactive Picker inside a List section header: functionally correct per SwiftUI, but visual alignment in the section header style (all-caps, small) may look unexpected — a human UI review should confirm the header rendering. Index-based identity (`\.offset`) used in ForEach because Ingredient has no stable ID; this is safe for a non-mutable, display-only list.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should write unit tests covering: toggle gathered state, scaled quantity display for .number/.text/nil quantities, empty state branch, and gathered row strikethrough + secondary foreground styling.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — this is a new file with no overlap with sibling beads.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used `ingredients: [Ingredient]` parameter (not full Recipe) to match sibling view patterns (RecipeStatStrip takes `metadata: Metadata`). Used `Set<Int>` keyed by index for gathered state since Ingredient has no Identifiable conformance. Used `AnyShapeStyle` for conditional foregroundStyle calls to satisfy Swift's type checker. Picker uses `.menu` style to keep the header row compact.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Visual aspects (Picker position in header, strikethrough rendering, empty state centering) cannot be verified without UI test or manual inspection. Logic paths (toggle, scale application, nil quantity hiding) are unit-testable.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Ingredient rows use index-based identity — if the ingredient list were mutable and reordered, gathered state would shift incorrectly. For this read-only display view the risk is zero.

conflict_risks: None — this is a new file with no overlap with sibling beads.
